source_evidence.basis: public schema contrast error behavior isolated from upstream fix patch

build.dependency_mode: per-revision locked test-target Manifest.toml + pinned Julia binary

review.summary: The commit fixes a real defect in schema.jl where passing `:x => DummyCoding` (a type instead of an instance) was a footgun that previously errored but stopped erroring due to another fix. The production change adds a specific method to catch this case and restore the error. The issue body confirms existing behavior was violated (the error path disappeared) and needed to be restored.
review.evidence: Issue #283 explicitly states 'a fix to one issue caused a previously erroring path to no longer error. I restored the error with a specific method to catch the footgun of passing `:x => DummyCoding` (instead of `:x => DummyCoding()`) earlier.' The production file src/schema.jl is modified alongside test file changes. The commit subject says 'fix tests on nightly' which references restoring correct behavior.
review.missing_evidence: Cannot see the actual diff to confirm the exact nature of the production code change in schema.jl. The fix is partially motivated by test infrastructure changes (@test_broken behavior on nightly) which adds some ambiguity about whether this is purely a bug fix or partly test maintenance.
review.validation_risks: The fix is partially driven by test infrastructure changes (Julia nightly changing @test_broken semantics), which means some test changes may be adapting to upstream rather than testing a bug fix. The two drop_term test changes appear to be semantic acceptance of changed behavior rather than bug fixes. Only the DummyCoding type vs instance footgun restoration is clearly a production bug fix.
review.suggested_tests: Test that passing a contrast type (e.g., `:x => DummyCoding`) instead of an instance (`:x => DummyCoding()`) throws an appropriate error. Test that passing a proper instance works correctly.
